Mazda Launches 2027 CX-90 in the States, Crossover Is Basically the Same but a Bit Different
13 photos
Photo: Mazda
In production since 2023, the Mazda CX-90 has now entered the 2027 model year in the United States of America, where the company’s local branch has just announced the novelties and pricing details.
Since you probably want to find out what is new, we will start by telling you that the updated rear suspension bushings are part of the novelties, and these, together with the revised rear suspension crossmember, are said to deliver improved comfort over rough surfaces.
Four new exterior paint colors have also joined the palette, and these are called the Zircon Sand Metallic, Melting Copper Metallic, Navy Blue Mica, and Aero Grey Metallic. Last but not least, the 3.3 Turbo Premium Sport and the 3.3 Turbo S Premium Sport can now be configured with two rows of seats, making the CX-90 replace the CX-70 in the United States of America.
But what about the pricing, you ask? Well, the 2027 Mazda CX-90 now starts at $39,700 for the base 3.3 Turbo Select, which is $400 more than the equivalent 2026 model year grade. It features a 7-inch TFT display, a 10.25-inch infotainment system, an eight-speaker audio system, smartphone integration, push-button start, advanced keyless entry, a three-zone automatic climate control system, LED exterior lights, 19-inch wheels, and a few other things.
Photo: Mazda Power is supplied by a 3.3-liter turbocharged inline-six, which features 48-volt mild-hybrid assistance, and produces 280 hp (284 s/209 kW) and 332 lb-ft (450 Nm) of torque on 87-octane fuel. An eight-speed automatic transmission delivers everything to the standard i-Activ all-wheel drive system. Radar-guided cruise control with stop and go, blind spot monitoring, rear cross traffic alert, lane departure warning, driver attention alert, and other safety features are also on deck.
Mazda’s 2027 CX-90 3.3 Turbo Preferred is next, and starts at $43,850. It is also $400 more expensive over the previous model year, and adds stuff such as the 21-inch wheels, some piano black accents on the outside, roof rails, heated and ventilated front seats, heated second-row seating, an 8-way power-adjustable driver’s seat with power lumbar support and memory setting, an 8-way power-adjustable front passenger seat, a heated steering wheel, a 12.3-inch infotainment system, and a few other bits and bobs.
The 2026 3.3 Turbo Premium Sport version of the Mazda CX-90 used to start at $47,480, and can now be ordered from $46,880 for the 2027 model year with two rows of seats, or $48,080 with three rows. It can also be ordered with second-row captain’s chairs, and features different 21-inch wheels, some tweaks on the outside, piano black door mirror head covers, piano black roof rails, standard Alexa Built-In, and a few other things.
Mazda’s CX-90 3.3 Turbo Premium Plus comes next, carrying an MSRP of $50,670 for the 2027 model year, up from last year’s $50,270. It features more advanced headlights, Mazda Online Navigation with over-the-air updates, black or white Nappa leather upholstery, foot lamp illumination, and a 150-watt outlet in the cargo area. A 360-degree view monitor with see-through view and trailer hitch view, front cross traffic alert, and others are also on deck.
For the 2027 CX-90 PHEV Preferred, which features an electrified 2.5-liter naturally aspirated four-cylinder engine and a 17.8 kWh battery pack, and has 323 hp (327 ps/240 kW) and 369 lb-ft (500 Nm) of torque combined, you are looking at a minimum of $50,695, which is the same as the previous model year. It has an electric driving range of up to 27 miles (43 km), has Sport, Off-Road, and EV drive modes, 21-inch wheels, a power sunroof, a power tailgate, heated side mirrors, full LED lighting, rain-sensing wipers, etc.
Photo: Mazda Ventilated front seats, two-position memory for the driver’s seat, three-zone climate control, heated steering wheel, a 12.3-inch TFT LCD instrument panel display, a 12.3-inch infotainment system, wireless charging pads, more USB-C ports, wireless smartphone integration, front and rear parking sensors, and other stuff are also mentioned as being standard.
The PHEV Premium Sport version of the 2027 Mazda CX-90 comes from $55,500, which is also the same as before, and adds auto-dimming side mirrors with automatic power folding, a head-up display, a frameless and auto-dimming rearview mirror with HomeLink, a Bose sound system, and a few other features are also included here.
Mazda’s 2027 CX-90 PHEV Premium Plus starts at $58,700, unchanged from the previous model year, brings different 21-inch wheels, some tweaks on the outside, adaptive front lights, heated side mirrors with memory and tilt-down in reverse, Mazda Online Navigation, Nappa leather upholstery, and the usual safety gizmos, in addition to other stuff.
The 2027 Mazda CX-90 Turbo S Premium Sport, which packs an e-Skyactiv G 3.3-liter inline-six turbocharged engine, rated at 340 hp (345 ps/254 kW) and 369 lb-ft (488 Nm) of torque, starts at $53,540. It has Sport, Off-Road, and Towing modes, a blackout exterior theme, heated and ventilated seats, a heated steering wheel, black or white Nappa leather, etc. The 3.3 Turbo S Premium Plus kicks off at $57,970, and rounds off the offering with a bit more gear.
